instructions: Slice the mushrooms 1/4 inch thick. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic. Cut the tomatoes in half and grate them on the big holes of a box grater into a bowl, then throw away the skins. That should be about 1 cup.
Bring the broth to a simmer in a small pot and keep it on low heat.
Heat the oil in a wide, deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and starting to turn golden.

Add the mushrooms, the pepper, 1/2 tsp of the salt, the cinnamon stick and the bay leaf. Turn the heat up to medium-high and cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mushrooms are browned and the liquid has cooked off.
Add the garlic and the orzo. Stir for 1 minute, until the orzo is coated in oil and smells toasty.
Pour in the wine and cook for 1 minute, until most of it has cooked off. Add the grated tomato, the hot broth and the last 1/4 tsp salt, and stir.

Turn the heat to medium and simmer without a lid for 10 minutes, stirring every minute or two, until the orzo is tender and the sauce is thick and creamy. If it gets dry before the orzo is cooked, add a splash of hot water.
Take the pan off the heat. Fish out the cinnamon stick and bay leaf, and stir in half the Pecorino Romano.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve in bowls topped with the rest of the Pecorino Romano and the basil, torn.
method_notes: No version of this exact dish has 20 ratings, so this follows Maria Loi's mushroom kritharaki from The Greek Diet (tomato and mushrooms, orzo toasted and cooked risotto style), the closest match to the list line. It is the stovetop version trimmed to about 32 minutes for 4: the onion is softened rather than caramelized and the orzo toasts in the same pan as the mushrooms. Kalofagas and Marilena's Kitchen confirm the one-pan, hot broth, orzo-in-the-sauce method. Maria Loi's pecorino is kept (animal rennet, so a stricter vegetarian may want a vegetarian hard cheese).
